newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices jolted higher by reminder of low stocks.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices jolted higher by reminder of low stocks.

text.p: Oil prices were jolted higher on Thursday as data from the United States reminded traders that heating oil stocks remained low with winter far from over.
North Sea Brent crude, the price marker for international trade, rose 33 cents a barrel on the London futures market to $22.81 by 1718 GMT.

U.S. government data confirmed weekly figures released on Wednesday by oil companies there, and showed that distillate stocks, including heating oil, fell by 4.8 million barrels last week and crude stocks fell by 1.5 million.
Historically low stocks have haunted the market over the last year -- a result of oil companies' policy of running down inventory to shave costs.
That has left prices vulnerable to short-term weather shocks or supply disruption, which boosted the market to a six-year high of $25 for Brent hit in October.
Despite forecasts of a further cold snap for the U.S. Midwest at the weekend, the weather was seen less of an immediate factor on Thursday than the fear of supply glitches.
Traders said the market twitched higher after Kurdish rebels attacked a major pipeline carrying Iraqi crude across Turkey to a Mediterranean terminal.
The attack failed to stop the flow of oil, exported from sanctions-bound Iraq under the terms of the United Nations agreement to fund humanitarian aid.

A fire at Tosco Corp's refinery near San Francisco which killed one and injured 25, closed two refining units there. Traders also noted that a New Jersey refinery also owned by Tosco had cut its gasoline output by a half after a fire on Friday.
